chapter: Fellow musicians: Kirk, Bunk, Parker, McShann
title: Bunk Johnson sitting in at the Yellow Front
summary: Lovett says Bunk sat in rather than led, was paid, and did not stay long; Lovett never spent time in New Orleans.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Then some years later Bunk Johnson came up but he wasn't in town long but he stayed in town long enough for you to play with him?
That's right.
He was playing at the Yellow Front?
That's right.
Was he playing as a side man or was he leading?
No, he just --
Was he the leader of the band?
No, he wasn't the leader of the band.
He was a side man?
Yeah, he just sat in, you know.
Oh, he just sat in. Well, he had to eat, you know. He had to work for...
This was the easiest thing at the
Yellow Front.
Back in those days, yeah.
But did he get paid? I mean, how did he live?
Sure.
I see.
He didn't stay a long time, you know what I mean.
Well, that's the story of your playing with Bunk. I wondered about that because you didn't spend any time in New Orleans at all, did you? You went from Shreveport to Kansas City, Baby?
That's right. No, I didn't stay in New Orleans very long.
